name: Análisis de Marcadores Discursivos
description: Analyzes the usage patterns of discourse markers (connectives, transitions) to differentiate AI-generated from human-written text.
useCase: Detecting AI text through overuse or underuse of cohesive discourse connectives
mechanism: Identifies and quantifies discourse markers (e.g., 'however', 'therefore', 'furthermore', 'in addition') and their positional distribution within texts. AI-generated text typically exhibits a narrower set of discourse markers with more formulaic placement patterns. The method constructs a discourse marker profile and compares it against human reference distributions using Jensen-Shannon divergence.
source: Kumarage et al. (2023) - Stylometric Detection of AI-Generated Text in Twitter Timelines, arXiv
algorithm: Discourse Marker Extraction + Positional Analysis + Distribution Comparison
parameters: Marker lexicon: 150+ markers, Position tracking: sentence-initial/medial/final, Frequency normalization: per-sentence, Comparison: JSD metric
strengths:
• Captures high-level text organization patterns
• Robust across different text lengths
• Linguistically interpretable features
• Complements token-level detection methods
limitations:
• Marker inventory varies across languages
• Genre-dependent baseline distributions
• Advanced LLMs can produce varied discourse patterns
• Requires careful marker taxonomy definition

references.title: Kumarage, T. et al. (2023). Stylometric Detection of AI-Generated Text in Twitter Timelines. arXiv.
Halliday, M. A. K. & Hasan, R. (1976). Cohesion in English. Longman.
Zellers, R. et al. (2019). Defending Against Neural Fake News. NeurIPS.
